name: AWS DMS
oneLiner: Migrate and continuously replicate (CDC) databases into AWS.
whatItIs: AWS Database Migration Service moves data from a source database to a target, either as a one-time migration or as ongoing change-data-capture (CDC) replication. It reads the source's transaction log and applies inserts/updates/deletes to the target continuously, keeping them in sync with minimal load and downtime. In a data platform, DMS is the bridge that gets operational data out of OLTP databases (RDS, on-prem, other clouds) and into the analytics world — S3, Redshift or another database — without pausing the source. It also handles heterogeneous migrations (e.g. Oracle → PostgreSQL), often paired with the Schema Conversion Tool.

inPractice.narrative: A production PostgreSQL database holds live orders. Analytics needs that data, but querying production is off-limits. DMS does an initial full load of the tables into S3/Redshift, then switches to CDC — tailing the database's write-ahead log and streaming every change into the lake in near-real-time. Analysts get fresh data to query while the app's database is untouched. DMS is the replication pipe between the operational source and the analytical target.

coreConcepts.detail: DMS first bulk-copies existing data (full load), then continuously applies ongoing changes via change-data-capture, so the target stays current with minimal source impact.
CDC reads the source's transaction log to capture inserts/updates/deletes as they happen — near-real-time replication without querying tables repeatedly.
Same-engine moves (PostgreSQL→PostgreSQL) are straightforward; cross-engine (Oracle→PostgreSQL) needs schema conversion (SCT/DMS Schema Conversion) for types and code.
A replication instance (or DMS Serverless) runs the task; you size it for throughput, or let serverless auto-scale capacity.
Targets include S3 (as files for the lake), Redshift, Kinesis, OpenSearch and databases — making DMS a common lake-ingestion tool, not just a DB-to-DB mover.
Table mappings and lightweight transformations select and reshape what's replicated (filtering rows, renaming) during the move.

whenToUse: Continuously replicating OLTP data into S3/Redshift for analytics (CDC).
Migrating databases to AWS with minimal downtime.
Heterogeneous migrations (e.g. Oracle → Aurora PostgreSQL) with schema conversion.
Keeping a lake/warehouse in near-real-time sync with source databases.
Streaming DB changes to Kinesis/OpenSearch for downstream use.
whenNotToUse: Bulk file/object transfer (not databases) — use DataSync.
Heavy in-flight transformation — land the data then transform with Glue/EMR.
One-off flat-file loads where a simple COPY/ingest is enough.
Streaming event ingestion from apps — that's Kinesis/MSK, not DMS.

keyFacts.label: Modes
keyFacts.value: Full load, full load + CDC, or CDC-only.

keyFacts.label: Targets
keyFacts.value: S3, Redshift, Kinesis, OpenSearch, databases, etc.

keyFacts.label: Billing
keyFacts.value: Per replication instance-hour (or serverless capacity) + storage/transfer.

pricingShape: DMS bills for the replication instance running the task — per-hour by instance size — plus log/storage and data transfer; DMS Serverless instead bills by capacity units consumed. Because CDC tasks run continuously to stay in sync, an ongoing replication has a steady cost proportional to the instance size you provision. Levers: right-size the replication instance to throughput, use serverless for variable loads, and stop tasks/instances you no longer need. The Schema Conversion Tool itself is free; the cost is the replication compute.
gotchas: CDC requires source-side settings (e.g. logical replication / supplemental logging) — miss them and CDC silently can't capture changes.
An under-sized replication instance falls behind on high-change-rate sources, growing replication lag.
Heterogeneous migrations need schema conversion; DMS moves data, not complex stored procedures/code.
It does light transformation only — don't try to reshape heavily in DMS; land then transform.
Continuous CDC tasks run (and bill) 24/7 — track and stop ones no longer needed.

equivalents.name: Datastream
equivalents.note: Serverless CDC into BigQuery/Cloud Storage; GCP's change-replication analogue.
